chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim and Abī Qatādah, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man whose garment falls upon a dead donkey: is salat (prayer) valid in it before he washes it? He said: Washing it is not required of him; let him perform salat (prayer) in it, and there is no harm.

So the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it to mean that when a year has passed over that and it has become bone, then washing the garment because of it is not obligatory. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer); the act of worship whose validity is under discussion
key_terms.ثَوْبُهُ: his garment; the clothing whose purity status is being asked about
key_terms.حِمَارٍ مَيِّتٍ: a dead donkey; the carcass mentioned in the legal question
key_terms.سَنَةٌ: a year; the period after which the carcass is understood to have decomposed
key_terms.عَظْمًا: bone; indicating the decomposed state relevant to the ruling
key_terms.غَسْلُهُ: washing it; cleaning the garment after contact
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in a garment that touched a dead animal before washing it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling about a garment coming into contact with a dead donkey and whether salat (prayer) in it is valid before washing. The report states that washing is not required, and the compiler then explains that this is to be understood in a case where the carcass has decomposed and become bone, such that the garment does not require washing from it.
